introduction.title: Welcome!
introduction.content:
The Cavic Pre-Festival Workshops 2026 are a prelude to the main festival, offering participants immersive, hands-on experiences at the intersection of art, technology, and culture. This year's workshops bring together distinguished speakers who will guide participants through collaborative creation, strategic thinking, and cultural innovation.

Whether you're an artist exploring digital tools, a technologist seeking creative applications, or a cultural practitioner looking to scale your impact, these workshops provide the space to learn, experiment, and connect with a vibrant community of innovators.

speakers.name: Dr. Lanre Phillips
speakers.bio:
Dr. Lanre Phillips is a seasoned professional with over 25 years of experience spanning FMCG, Banking, and Telecommunications industries. His expertise in social enterprise has led him to work with numerous business hubs, incubators, and accelerators across Africa, particularly in Nigeria.

Dr. Phillips holds a passionate belief in small business growth through human capacity development and strategic business implementation. His approach focuses on operational excellence and value creation through people-centered strategies.

As a faculty member of several training organizations, he specializes in:
• Business Strategy
• Storytelling
• Organisational Behaviour
• Business Branding
• Customer Service
• Leadership
• Sales Techniques
• Entrepreneurship

His notable achievements include:
• Member of the Global Entrepreneurship Network, Nigeria team
• Board member of the Integrated Institute of Professional Management (IIPM)
• Key contributor to projects like You WIN, World Bank's Women X Programme, and the Road to Growth by the Cherie Blaire Foundation

Education:
• Doctorate in Business Administration (DBA) - Swiss Management Centre
• MSc Economics - University of Jos
• MBA - University of Jos
• Bachelor's in Economics - University of Ibadan (1995)

speakers.name: Marta Verde Baqueiro
speakers.bio:
Marta Verde Baqueiro is a visual artist, creative technologist and educator working at the intersection of live performance, real-time media systems and embodied interaction. Her practice focuses on creating responsive environments where sound, light and visuals react to human movement, signal input and physical space.

She currently works as Associate Faculty at Berklee College of Music (Valencia Campus) and is a Max/MSP Certified Trainer. Her work explores hybrid performance ecosystems combining sensors, creative coding, analog video synthesis and digital fabrication, often bridging organic processes and electronic systems.

As a faculty member and mentor, she specializes in:
• Hybrid performance & responsive environments
• Sensors, embodied interaction & realtime media
• Creative coding (Max/MSP, Processing, realtime systems)
• Experimental audiovisual performance & installation
• Cross-disciplinary workshop and lab facilitation

Her notable achievements include:
• Forbes España Top 100 Most Creative People in Business (2024)
• First Prize — We:Now Awards (Music Category) for Espectro Dorado
• Alumni Award — Universidade de Vigo (2025)
• Maker of Merit — Maker Faire Galicia (2025)
• Presentations at Ars Electronica, Sónar +D, MIRA Festival, LEV Festival and Primavera Sound

Academic Background:
• Associate Faculty — Berklee College of Music (Valencia Campus)
• Lecturer — Master in Sonology, Conservatorio Superior de Música Joaquín Rodrigo
• Lecturer — BAU College of Arts and Design, Barcelona
• Fab Academy digital fabrication program

speakers.name: Faith Ono
speakers.bio:
Faith Ono is a Community and Programs Manager and a strategic leader within the African startup ecosystem. As the Program and Partnerships Manager at The Enablers Network, she oversees the initiatives of the community that powers Founders Friday, one of Abuja's largest monthly founder meetups. Her expertise lies in building operational frameworks, steering strategic business directions, and managing multidisciplinary teams to drive collaboration and growth.

At the June CAVIC workshop, Faith serves as a lead facilitator, specializing in community dynamics and collaborative structures:
Team Formation & Synergy: She manages the critical process of grouping participants into balanced pods, ensuring a productive "marriage" between diverse artistic and technical disciplines.
Creative Energizing: Faith facilitates sessions designed to spark cross-discipline pairing and idea-sharing, helping participants communicate their visions effectively.
Strategic Matchmaking: She guides the "Idea Pitch Circle," ensuring that projects are anchored in shared resonance and that each team maintains a balanced ratio of creative to technical hands.
Her role is essential in transforming a group of individual practitioners into a cohesive community ready to build the next generation of immersive experiences.

speakers.name: Ugochukwu David Ogbuehi
speakers.role: Creative Technologist, Immersive Arts Producer & Curator
speakers.bio:
Ugochukwu David Ogbuehi is a combined arts practitioner, creative technologist, and immersive arts producer whose work bridges live performance, virtual environments, and accessible design. Based in London, his practice brings together projection mapping, Unreal Engine, haptic sound, and creative computing to build sensory-rich experiences for diverse audiences, with a strong research focus on accessibility for d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities.

David's work spans curation, production, and technical delivery across theatre, installation, and public arts programming. As a core member of TCMO (The Collective Members Only), he has led multidisciplinary projects that create opportunities for emerging artists, including immersive public-facing collaborations with Boundless Theatre, Crystal Palace Park Trust, and the Southbank Centre.

As a technologist and producer, he specializes in:
• Immersive technology and virtual environment design
• Projection mapping and realtime media systems
• Spatial sound, haptic audio and live event production
• Creative computing with Python and Arduino
• Inclusive design for live performance and public engagement

His notable achievements include:
• Key Project Manager and Artist Liaison for TCMO x Boundless: Box in the Park (2025)
• Technical Assistant (Audio) on Lost Text/Found Space's Far Away at Ambika P3, contributing to a 14-speaker audio setup on a production nominated for 6 Fringe Theatre awards
• Motion Graphics and VFX Artist for Opera Greenwich's production of The Magic Flute (2025)
• Inclusive design researcher on Deaf Rave x Kinda Studios' Resonance project, exploring haptic technology for d/Deaf audiences
• Producer and Curator for Fear & Faith I as part of The Albany's Revolution Through Music programme

Academic Background:
• MA Art and Emerging Technologies — University of Westminster
• MSc Digital Marketing — Robert Gordon University
• BSc Computer Science — Babcock University
